post.summary: Upload a CSV of IP/MAC matches as user ARP records.
post.description:
The records are accepted for processing and are not queryable yet when this endpoint responds.

The file is validated as a whole: the first unusable line rejects the entire upload and no record is applied. If saving the records fails midway the upload may have been applied in part, in which case re-uploading the same file is safe and converges to the full result.

### Required scopes:
* `PERMISSION.DEVICE.MANAGE`

400.description: The file cannot be used. No record was applied.

413.description: The file must be at most 10485760 bytes.

502.description: Failed to save the ARP records. The file was not applied in full; retry the upload.

line.title: Line
line.description: The number of the line in the file that was rejected.

column.title: Column
column.description: The name of the column that was rejected.

error.title: Error
error.description: A description of the problem with the value.

ArpUploadError.title: ArpUploadError
ArpUploadError.description:
The reason an ARP records upload was rejected.

The upload is rejected as a whole, so none of the records in the file were applied. Only problems
that are specific to a single line carry `line`, `column`, `value` and `error`.

examples.message: The file must have a header row with the columns "ip" and "mac".

examples.error: IPv6 addresses are not supported; only IPv4.

file.title: File
file.description: A CSV file with the columns ip,mac.

expiration.title: Expiration
expiration.description: The UTC time at which the uploaded records expire. Must be in the future and at most 30 days from now.

network_id.title: Network Id
network_id.description: Identifies the logical network segment the ARP data originates from. Used to disambiguate overlapping IP ranges across different network segments. When multiple networks share the same IP space, this field ensures MAC-to-IP bindings are resolved within the correct network context.

ArpUploadRequest.title: ArpUploadRequest
ArpUploadRequest.description: A CSV of IP/MAC matches to upload as user ARP records.

total_rows.title: Total Rows
total_rows.description: The number of data rows in the file. Blank rows are not counted.

accepted_records.title: Accepted Records
accepted_records.description: The number of ARP records that were sent for processing.

duplicate_rows.title: Duplicate Rows
duplicate_rows.description: The number of rows that repeated an earlier IP/MAC match and were skipped.

expiration.title: Expiration
expiration.description: The UTC time at which the uploaded records expire.

ArpUploadResponse.title: ArpUploadResponse
ArpUploadResponse.description: A summary of an accepted ARP records upload.

asset_id.title: Asset Id
asset_id.description:
The identifier that will be used to find the asset that needs to be updated.

The content type will vary according to the selected `asset_id_source` field (e.g. IP v4, Asset ID, etc.).

Generally speaking, all identifiers except Asset ID are provided by the customer's environment.

key.title: Key
key.description:
The key of the asset you wish to update.
* Currently, only custom properties are supported.
* For custom properties, add the `custom.` prefix. (e.g. `custom.MY_CUSTOM_PROPERTY`).
* To see the available custom properties, please refer to the [List all device custom property configurations](/reference/get_settings_device_custom_properties_get#/) endpoint.

get.summary: Get the URLs of the latest data exports of a particular entity.
get.description:
Each `time_frame_days` value of an entity is exported separately, so
`applications` with `time_frame_days=7` and `applications` with `time_frame_days=30` are two independent exports
that are enabled, disabled and read on their own. Omitting `time_frame_days` addresses the entity's default window.

| Entity | Supported `time_frame_days` | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `applications` | 2, 7, 14, 30 | 30 |  |
| `device-delete-events` | 2, 7, 14, 30, 90 | 14 |  |
| `device-merge-events` | 2, 7, 14, 30, 90 | 14 |  |
| `ip-connections` | 1-7 | - | accepted when reading, to pick the aggregation date; cannot be set when enabling the export |
| `risk-factors` | 2, 7, 14, 30 | 30 |  |
| `vulnerabilities` | 2, 7, 14, 30 | 30 |  |

### Required scopes:
* `PERMISSION.REPORT.READ`
* `FULL_VISIBILITY`

| `risk-factors` | 2, 7, 14, 30 | 30 |  |
| `vulnerabilities` | 2, 7, 14, 30 | 30 |  |

source_data_timestamp.title: Source Data Timestamp
source_data_timestamp.description: When the exported data was last refreshed at the source. Use it to tell how fresh the rows are, as opposed to `urls_creation_time`, which is when the export files themselves were produced. `null` when the export has not run yet or the source did not report a timestamp.
